newsitem.title: FINLAND: Salomon sees intermediaries' role declining in EMU.
newsitem.headline: Salomon sees intermediaries' role declining in EMU.

text.p: The role of capital market intermediaries will decline in EMU as issuers get new opportunities to raise money and investors seek higher yields, Salomon Brother's adviser Graham Bishop said on Wednesday.

Bishop told an EMU seminar arranged by training institute IIR Finland that the government debt yield level in EMU would likely decline as the ageing European population, concerned with their own pensions, would make up an increasing portion of the electorate and investors would seek higher yields from riskier securities.
Technological change would help bring investors closer to issuers, and a wave of securitisation was likely, he said.
"I think it will be possible to do the complete disintermediation, the direct contact between the borrower and investor will happen," Bishop said.
"Virtual dealers" could operate anywhere on non-government debt markets which would be "tremendously deep and liquid", he said.
For most Finnish corporate issuers, whose name recognition in not what flagship Nokia enjoys, rating would be the key to find investors across Europe, he said.

Bishop also said that despite current jitters, he expected "a broad EMU which will start on time, endure and enlarge", due to Europe's committment, and the fact that strong economic trends now favour decisions on further integration.
